idea-plugin.name: RefIo
idea-plugin.description:
RefIo - Local-First AI Coding Plugin for IntelliJ.

For developers who want the leverage of AI coding without giving up observability, model choice, or the native JetBrains experience.

An open-source AI coding plugin for IntelliJ IDEA, built in Kotlin. Native JetBrains UI, no WebView, no cloud account required, no telemetry. Works with local models (Ollama, LM Studio) or cloud LLMs.

Early-stage, actively developed. The foundation is in place: three execution modes, visible tool calls, a snapshot before every write and a build check after it. The orchestration depth is still growing. See the Roadmap for where the project is heading.

What it does today

  • Three execution modes - Chat (conversation, no tools), Plan (read-only analysis, enforced in code), Agent (file edits with a snapshot before every write).
  • Verified edits - after a turn that changed files, RefIo runs your build or test command, feeds the real failures back to the model for up to two repair rounds, and marks the turn as failed verification instead of reporting a success it cannot back up.
  • Local or cloud LLMs - Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Custom OpenAI, Z.AI. A universal tool-calling protocol works with models that lack native function calling.
  • Guardrails for small models - loop and repetition detection, no-op edit detection, and an abandoned turn recorded as incomplete rather than successful.
  • Structural refactoring - find_usages and rename_symbol backed by IntelliJ PSI inside the IDE.
  • Tool system - per-mode permissions (ON / ASK / OFF), a diff preview before an edit is approved, PathSandbox with symlink resolution, regex allow/block/ask command rules, snapshot and rollback.
  • Context control - @mentions for directing context (@file, @codebase, @diff, @problems, @terminal, and more), RAG with semantic chunking, a token budget that scales to the model's context window.
  • Cost control - per-session cost ceiling, reasoning-effort levels, and cache-aware accounting so a cache-served prompt is not billed as fresh.
  • Extensibility - subagents as Markdown + YAML (Claude Code compatible format), MCP protocol support (STDIO + HTTP/SSE) with built-in presets, project instructions via AGENTS.md and .refio/rules/*.md with glob-based activation.
  • One core, three surfaces - the native IntelliJ plugin, a full terminal TUI and a headless runner share the same engine, so an agent run can be scripted and asserted on.
  • No-egress mode - one switch blocks all outbound traffic, both model calls and the web tools, for strict offline work.

What it is, and what it isn't

It is: an early-stage open-source plugin with a clear direction - a native JetBrains tool for developers working in Kotlin, Java and JVM ecosystems, or anyone who wants their AI coding agent to run offline and be auditable.

It isn't: a drop-in replacement for inline completion (different category). A polished enterprise-grade product (not yet). Something you install and forget - changes happen fast at v0.0.1.x.

Known limitations (honest)

  • No git worktree isolation per task - agents edit your working tree directly, with snapshot rollback.
  • The planning loop is basic - no plan-refinement iteration yet.
  • The multi-agent runtime works but can only be launched from the CLI; the IDE visualizes a run, it does not start one.
  • Security layers are pragmatic and self-assessed, not independently audited.
  • Tested on IntelliJ IDEA only; other JetBrains IDEs may work but are not claimed.
  • Small commit history, fast changes, breaking changes possible pre-1.0.

Quick start with local models

ollama pull nomic-embed-text        # required for RAG
ollama pull qwen3.5:9b              # small and fast
# or, for bigger hardware:
ollama pull qwen3.5:35b
ollama pull qwen3.5:122b
  1. Install the plugin from JetBrains Marketplace
  2. Open the RefIo tool window (right sidebar)
  3. Go to RefIo, Settings and pick your model
  4. Start with @codebase your question here

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.2 or newer (Community or Ultimate)
  • Ollama or LM Studio (optional, for local models)
  • JDK 17+ only if you also want to build the standalone CLI
